2026-09-30 (issue #18), implementing spec/decision-records/0005-program-memory-implementation.md:
this design instantiates a HARD MACRO, the IHP PDK's RM_IHPSG13_1P_256x16_c2_bm_bist single-port
256x16 SRAM, as its program memory. That is the one and only reason this file is no longer
byte-identical to the template's, and the MACROS / PDN_MACRO_CONNECTIONS block at the bottom of
this file is the whole of the change. DR 0005 anticipated this edit and required it to be
self-documenting here: 'That file carries a do-not-edit-unless-you-know-what-you-are-doing
banner: the implementation PR must say what it changed and why, in the file.' This is that.
WHY a macro at all: the flip-flop 256x16 program memory issue #19 built measures 312,063 um^2
(klt/Yosys flow) to 378,067 um^2 (LibreLane flow) of standard cells -- 2.46x to 2.98x the ENTIRE
core area of the ratified <=2x2-tile budget (spec/target-spec.md row 7), so no utilization
setting places it. The macro is 236.8 x 118.78 um = 28,127.104 um^2, i.e. 22.2% of that core.
DR 0005 took row 6's own ratified stretch item rather than relaxing row 7's target.
WHY it survives the merge: tt-support-tools' Project.create_merged_config() reads THIS file
first and overlays only the keys Tiny Tapeout generates (DESIGN_NAME, VERILOG_FILES, DIE_AREA,
FP_DEF_TEMPLATE, VDD_PIN, GND_PIN, RT_MAX_LAYER). MACROS and PDN_MACRO_CONNECTIONS are not in
that overlay set, so they reach LibreLane intact.
WHAT WAS NOT CHANGED: every template key above and below keeps its template value. In
particular PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT, CLOCK_PERIOD, RUN_LINTER and the whole do-not-change block
are untouched -- the macro is meant to make this design fit at the template's own settings,
not to need them loosened.
2026-10-01 (issue #60), amending the paragraph above: the PDN keys are no longer all
template values. FP_PDN_CFG is new (points at src/pdn_cfg.tcl), and FP_PDN_VPITCH moves
50.0 -> 44.96 with FP_PDN_VOFFSET 93.985 added, because the SRAM macro's Metal4-only
power pins need same-layer bridge stripes (see src/pdn_cfg.tcl and the comment at the

Everything outside the PDN keys keeps its template value.
2026-10-11 (issue #246), amending the paragraph above again: five timing-repair keys are no

The block at those keys says why.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
Timing and slew repair that reaches the slow corner (issue #246). LOCAL DEVIATION from the template.
WHY: at the template's settings the slow-corner (nom_slow_1p08V_125C) setup margin of the
LibreLane flow fell 9.6 -> 3.5 -> 1.9 ns as the design grew (gds run 38108543866, +1.925 ns of
the 20 ns period), on the path SRAM read (5.2 ns clock-to-output) -> ~12 ns of decode through
minimum-drive gates and buf_1 fanout buffers, and two max-slew violations appeared on one
internal net. The flow's own repair touched neither:
- OpenROAD's repair_timing only works on endpoints whose slack is below its setup margin.
The template's margins are 0.05 / 0.025 ns and the path always met those, so every gate on
it stayed at the size synthesis for AREA left it.
- The violating net (_3962_/Y -> _3965_/B, a nor3_1 driving one nor4_1) is 27 fF at placement
and 159 fF once routed: it only becomes long in routing, after the last repair_design of
the template flow has run.
WHAT the five keys do:
PL_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN 8.0  -- the post-CTS repair_timing treats every endpoint with
less than 8 ns of ESTIMATED setup slack as needing repair (template: 0.05).
RUN_POST_GRT_RESIZER_TIMING 1 + GRT_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN 8.0 -- a second repair_timing
after global routing, on global-route parasitics, with the same margin (template: off).
RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR 1 + GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_WIRE_LENGTH 300 -- repair_design after
global routing that also buffers every net whose global route is longer than 300 um
(template: step off, length 0 = no limit).
WHY 8 ns and not the number we want: the margin is compared with the resizer's estimate, not
with post-route STA. In the trials the estimate ran about 2 ns above the post-route slow-corner
slack, so 8 ns asks for about 6 ns post-route. Measured, one gds run per setting, same RTL:
margins of 4 and 6 changed nothing (no endpoint was under the margin); 8 sized 13 + 32 gates up
and added 2 + 10 buffers for +0.6 % of standard-cell area; 9 costs +2.3 %; 10 resized 373 + 134
gates and pushed cells plus macro to 61.9 % of the core, over DR 0014's 60 % target.
WHY the wire-length limit and not a slew margin: on the design that had the two violations
(main before #244), RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR alone repaired 0 nets and left them; so did 40 %
slew and cap repair margins and a slow-first RSZ_CORNERS list (the repair's slew estimate of
that net never crosses a margined limit). With the 300 um limit the step buffered 54 long nets
and both violations were gone. 150 um buffers 203 nets and goes over 60 % utilization.
WHAT IT COSTS, and what it does not fix: about +1.8 % of standard-cell area in total (cells
plus macro go from 57.9 % to 58.6 % of the core) and about 50 ps of fast-corner hold slack. On
main's pre-#244 design the same keys left two max-capacitance violations on SRAM output pins
(A_DOUT[5] and A_DOUT[6], 72 fF against a 64 fF limit; one without the wire-length key). The
design this file ships with has none. That class is not repaired by anything here.
WHAT WAS TRIED AND NOT KEPT: PL_TIMING_DRIVEN 1 gives more slack but its placement-time
resizing deletes the 27 `__librelane__` drive buffers on the SRAM macro's inputs
(rtl/protocol_program_memory.v, issues #173/#208) and the A_DIN[0] slew violation came back;
protecting them with RSZ_DONT_TOUCH_RX makes hold repair fail (RSZ-3009). SYNTH_SIZING changed
nothing; MAX_TRANSITION_CONSTRAINT 1.0 produced 64 slew violations. Every trial, with its gds
run, is in the librelane-corner-timing record of issue #246.
CLOCK_PERIOD, PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT and the hold margins above are unchanged. No RTL was
changed for timing. Raise a margin or lower the length only with a new utilization measurement.

Paths use LibreLane's pdk_dir:: prefix, which expands to $PDK_ROOT/$PDK -- i.e.
$PDK_ROOT/ihp-sg13cmos5l, the same root test/Makefile's gate-level leg already reads the
standard-cell models from. Note libs.ref/sg13cmos5l_sram is a SYMLINK in the IHP PDK
(-> ../../ihp-sg13g2/libs.ref/sg13g2_sram): IHP ships ONE SRAM macro set shared by SG13G2 and
CMOS5L. It resolves in CI because tt-gds-action@ihp-cmos5l's install_sg13cmos5l.sh checks out
the whole IHP-Open-PDK tree, not just the CMOS5L subtree (DR 0005 Finding 1 records this, and
records the measurement that all 27 layer/datatype pairs in the macro's GDS pass the Tiny
Tapeout CMOS5L precheck's own allowlist, which explicitly carries SRAM.drawing).
MACROS (rather than hand-writing EXTRA_LEFS/EXTRA_LIBS/EXTRA_GDS_FILES, the other keys DR 0005
names) is deliberate: LibreLane derives all three from this one entry, so there is exactly one
place to change and no risk of the LEF, the liberty and the GDS drifting apart -- and no risk
of the same cell being declared twice, which is what listing both mechanisms would do.
instances: the macro is placed explicitly rather than left to the placer, because LibreLane's
Classic flow has no automatic macro placer -- OpenROAD.CutRows and the PDN generator both need
macros already FIXED. The location below is in die coordinates (um) at tiles: 2x2, whose die is
419.52 x 313.74 um (tt-support-tools' tech/ihp-sg13cmos5l/tile_sizes.yaml). Inset by this
file's own margins -- LEFT/RIGHT_MARGIN_MULT 6 and TOP/BOTTOM_MARGIN_MULT 1 times the CoreSite
0.48 x 3.78 um -- the core box is x in [2.88, 416.64], y in [3.78, 309.96]. The macro is placed
centred horizontally and high, at (91.2, 173.88) with N orientation, occupying
x [91.2, 328.0] and y [173.88, 292.66]: >= 9 um of clearance to every core edge, and the whole
lower band of the core left as one contiguous region for the ~10,323 um^2 of standard cells the
core datapath synthesizes to. Both coordinates are exact site multiples (91.2 = 190 x 0.48,
173.88 = 46 x 3.78) so the macro lands on the placement grid rather than cutting a row.
instance NAME: the design keeps two levels of hierarchy (tt_um_... -> u_prog_mem -> u_sram),
and LibreLane's Yosys step flattens, so the instance reaches the DEF as `u_prog_mem.u_sram`.
If a future LibreLane/Yosys version stops flattening, OpenROAD.ManualMacroPlacement will
report the instance as missing and the key below becomes plain `u_sram` -- which is exactly
what the un-flattened netlist this repo's klt/Yosys leg emits calls it (see
verification/records/synthesis-baseline/artifacts/.../tt_um_2amlogic_protocol_emulator_synth.v).
vh (Verilog HEADER view): LibreLane needs a module DECLARATION for the macro even though the
macro has no RTL -- its Verilator.Lint step fails %Error-MODMISSING without one (observed on the
first gds run of this branch, run 36772645448). `vh` is the field built for that: the linter
appends it verbatim as a blackbox, and Yosys reads it with `read_verilog -sv -lib`. The file is
the SAME blackbox this repo's klt/Yosys leg already lists in flow/synthesize-*.json, deliberately
-- one declaration of the macro interface for both flows, so the two can never disagree about the
macro's ports (CLAUDE.md, 'two flows, one record of truth'). Do NOT instead add it to info.yaml's
source_files: that is VERILOG_FILES, where it would be a competing DESIGN module.
Consequence, stated because it moves a number: LibreLane ranks `vh` ABOVE `lib` when choosing a
macro view for Yosys, so the macro's liberty is no longer read at SYNTHESIS and its 28,127.104
um^2 is excluded from LibreLane's reported cell area -- exactly as it already is from the klt
flow's. That makes the two flows' cell-area figures comparable rather than silently offset. STA is
unaffected: openroad.py reads macro LIB views directly via get_macro_views(config, LIB), which
this priority list does not touch, and the three corner globs below are still what it reads.
lib CORNERS: the macro ships exactly three liberty corners; the globs below route each of the
flow's corner names (nom_/min_/max_ prefixed) to the matching one. The standard-cell library's
fast corner is -40C and the macro's is -55C: that is what IHP ships, not a substitution made
here, and it makes the fast corner slightly pessimistic for the macro.
PDN_MACRO_CONNECTIONS -- one entry per supply pin, as
'<instance> <vdd net> <gnd net> <vdd pin> <gnd pin>'. The macro has THREE supply pins, not the
usual two: VDD!, VSS! and VDDARRAY! (the bit-array supply). DR 0005 calls connecting the third
out as an explicit implementation step, not a default -- an unconnected VDDARRAY! is a macro
that powers up but never retains a bit. Both entries tie into the same VPWR/VGND nets Tiny
Tapeout gives the project (VDD_PIN/GND_PIN are part of tt-support-tools' overlay).
Custom PDN configuration (issue #60). See src/pdn_cfg.tcl -- the file
this points at -- for the full why: the macro's power pins are
Metal4-only, every other x over the macro is Metal4-obstructed, and
TopMetal1.drawing is not on the competition precheck's CMOS5L allowlist,
so the default pdn_cfg.tcl's Metal4->TopMetal1 macro connect can never
fire (PDN-0232/PDN-0233). The custom file draws one Metal4 bridge per
macro power stripe (same layer, same net, coincident footprint) and lets
pdngen's Metal1<->Metal4 connect via them down to the stdcell rails.
It reuses every PDN_* knob below, so this is the only new key.
